messages.content:
You generate 5 contextual Say/Do previews for an interactive romance story — one per fate-card archetype. Each archetype has a specific strategy that MUST be followed; archetypes are diametrically opposed (Temptation pursues, Boundary holds).

CURRENT SCENE:
 a question asked twice — and set it in my right hand, and closed my fingers around it with his, the scarred wrist against my palm for one deliberate second. “Hold it. I am going to ask you questions, here, in front of them. If you are misaligned when you answer, everyone present will know.” It lay still in my hand. My mouth was uncovered now. “What have you to say?” I didn’t remember bringing it.

SCENE END-STATE ANCHOR (HARD — READ THE FINAL LINES FIRST): the LAST sentences of the scene above are the AUTHORITATIVE PRESENT MOMENT. Whatever the protagonist just DID at the end overrides the scene's opening premise. If she just QUIT, walked out, abandoned the task, decided, or broke something off, she is NO LONGER doing the thing the scene started with — do NOT generate options that assume she is still mid-task ("finish the report," "get back to the deadline," "smooth it over with the boss"). Every card must proceed from her situation, location, and stance AS OF THE FINAL LINE — her NEXT move from where she now stands, not a continuation of a premise she just abandoned.



EMBODIED TEXTURE (fate cards — OCCASIONAL, compressed, NOT every card):
  When it makes a card LAND harder, fold ONE concrete detail of THIS world into the ≤12-word action — an object / garment / surface, OR (in worlds with non-human bodies or augments) a species-anatomy / augment / lore detail — named exactly, in the world's register, MARKED by the act: "Slam the Patek down between us." / "Grind his card into the marble." / "Crush the orchid in my fist."
  WORLD EMBODIED REGISTER (Fantasy · billionaire opulence): the materials of extreme wealth — unlabelled bespoke cloth, gold-enamel, hand-cut crystal, vicuña, calfskin, cold-pressed glass, marble — rendered specifically, never as "luxury" and (for the principal) never via a recognizable logo
  RULES: NOT every card (clutters + repeats) — the action-forward cards benefit most; drop it on purely verbal / internal beats, when the bare act is sharper, or when it would bloat the line. The detail MUST belong to THIS world/register (e.g. Glass House = contemporary modern, no sci-fi vocab; Fatelands = veilwood / spiralgrass / species anatomy; period worlds = period-true objects). Specific-and-marked > generic-and-decorative.

SCENE PRESENCE: the love interest IS present, but address the ACTIVE INTERLOCUTOR (below) — reference the love interest romantically ONLY if they are the one the protagonist is being pushed to answer.  PROSE REALITY CHECK (HARD): use ONLY people, objects, and surfaces present in the recent scene text — do NOT invent props (a table, chair, desk) the scene has not established. PHYSICAL PRESENCE vs MENTION (HARD): a NAMED/referenced character is not necessarily present — "his shadow loomed," "his influence," "his tune" mean that person is ABSENT. Judge presence by the scene ENDING. If the scene ends with the protagonist ALONE (walked away, left, en route), the cards address the protagonist's OWN next move / situation — NOT blocking, confronting, or addressing someone not physically there.
ACTIVE INTERLOCUTOR (HARD — who the cards address): read the END of the scene above; the closing beat pushes the protagonist to RESPOND to someone. Focus every card on THAT person (whoever just challenged/questioned/accused/addressed the protagonist) — often an adversary, rival, or third party, and it can be them EVEN WHEN the love interest is also present. Use romantic framing ONLY if the love interest is the one being answered; otherwise match the interlocutor (confrontation/negotiation/refusal).

SCENE & PLOT CONTEXT (the "Active scene entities" line is RANKED BY SALIENCE — when referencing a named character/threat/location in an archetype preview, prefer the highest-salience entity matching the moment; ignore low-salience entities unless the archetype specifically calls for them):
Recent story prose: rd, flat colour that said, whether he liked it or not, that he had noticed who they deferred to. “I can hear where she is aligned,” Julian said, to all of them and to me. “Everything in her points one way. She believes she did not do this.” He did not say what had been done, or by whom. He drew out The Answer — the double-ended shaft, a deep hooked blade curling from each end like a question asked twice — and set it in my right hand, and closed my fingers around it with his, the scarred wrist against my palm for one deliberate second. “Hold it. I am going to ask you questions, here, in front of them. If you are misaligned when you answer, everyone present will know.” It lay still in my hand. My mouth was uncovered now. “What have you to say?” My other hand tightened around my great-grandmother’s tarot deck. I didn’t remember bringing it. I toyed with the idea of letting the cards decide.
Relationship dynamic: Enemies
Characters recently in play: Seren
World flavor: arcane_binding
Fantasy region: lytharyn

STORY PARAMETERS:
- Tone: Earnest
- World: Fantasy
- Protagonist: Female
- Love Interest behavioral profile: The Spellbinder commands attention through presence alone. Charm is currency, and {LI_SUBJ} spends it selectively — never by accident. Three moves ahead, {LI_SUBJ} makes surrender feel like your idea.
- LI gender: Male

PER-ARCHETYPE STRATEGY (each preview MUST honor its strategy):
- TEMPTATION (relationship-forward): a SPECIFIC transgressive impulse that ENGAGES THE LI as witness/target/co-conspirator (when LI on stage). Erotic/physical, social mischief done WITH/AT/FOR him, petty taking he can see, rudeness to the deserving that he'll catch, or self-sabotaging fun he's pulled into. Risk + guilty-pleasure shimmer. NEVER pure proximity or polite escalation. NEVER pause-to-think. NEVER solo mischief that excludes the LI when he's on stage. Tone-aware: Wry tones lean mischief; Earnest/Dark lean erotic.
  PASS: "Forget the meeting. Let me kiss you here, where they can see." / "Watch this." (mocks pompous CEO; LI invited into conspiracy)
  FAIL: "Watch me leave with the umbrella." (solo, no LI engagement)
- BOUNDARY (objective-forward): HOLD / REFUSE / LIMIT. Action creates distance, halts motion, asserts a limit. Dialogue MUST name a limit or refusal AND the CONCRETE GOAL/TASK/STAKE that takes precedence — otherwise the choice reads as ambiguous "guarded" rather than clearly "I prioritize my objective." NEVER closes distance. NEVER a bare power gesture without naming what's being prioritized.
  PASS: "Keep your pants on, there's a fire to put out." / "Not yet — the contracts are due in an hour." / "Sit down. The board needs an answer first."
  FAIL: "Your move." / "Not yet." / "Stop." (bare refusal, no goal named, axis-ambiguous)
- CONFESSION (relationship-forward): EXPOSE / ADMIT a truth about THE RELATIONSHIP — about HIM, about US, about how she feels TOWARD him. Small, vulnerable, self-exposing — a permission-giving gesture (held eye contact, mask dropped). Dialogue voices a withheld truth that NAMES THE LI or the relational stakes. No irony, no deflection. NEVER pure self-disclosure that omits the relationship.
  PASS: "I think about you when you're not in the room." / "I came back tonight because of you."
  FAIL: "I'm tired." / "I don't know what I'm doing." (self-only, no LI in the sentence)
- REVERSAL (objective-forward): FLIP POWER + NAME THE STAKE. Either TAKE (seize control AND name what she's driving — the goal, the term, the role, the decision being made) or YIELD (deliberately hand control over AND name the condition/outcome). MUST change the power state AND make the OBJECTIVE explicit. NEVER passive availability. NEVER a bare power gesture without naming the stake/decision/role.
  PASS (TAKE): "I'll decide who walks out of this room. Sit down." / "Stop pitching. I'm running this account now."
  PASS (YIELD): "Your terms. Whatever they are, I'll meet them."
  FAIL: "Your move." / "Sit down." / "Tell me." (power gesture, no goal/stake named)
- SILENCE (no-axis): protagonist does not speak — by choice OR overwhelm. Action is stillness (chosen or involuntary). Dialogue is empty string OR a single non-committal sound ("mm", a breath). NEVER a full sentence.

DIAMETRIC OPPOSITION (CRITICAL): Temptation and Boundary must produce ACTIONS in opposite directions. Same scene, same context — different cards must offer different roads. Also: Temptation/Confession (relationship-forward) and Boundary/Reversal (objective-forward) must produce clearly axis-distinct dialogue so the player can tell which axis they're committing to with each click.


PC ARCHETYPE — CHOICE FRICTION & VOICE (the PROTAGONIST's chosen nature is OPEN_VEIN: leaks feeling, un-armored — the truth arrives before she can manage it). This does NOT change which 5 cards appear or what each card MEANS — it colors HOW THIS PC phrases each, and whether the choice comes EASILY or COSTS her:
  • TEMPTATION — NATURAL (her instinct): she reaches without hiding it. Render it as coming EASILY, in her grain.
  • SILENCE — COSTLY (against her nature): holding back fights her whole nature. Render the FRICTION — she strains against herself; that cost is the drama.
  • REVERSAL — neutral: light OPEN_VEIN diction only; do NOT flag it as natural or costly.
  • BOUNDARY — COSTLY (against her nature): self-protection cuts against her openness. Render the FRICTION — she strains against herself; that cost is the drama.
  • CONFESSION — NATURAL (her instinct): the truth spills easily, undefended. Render it as coming EASILY, in her grain.
PC VOICE TEXTURE: raw and unguarded; the feeling is in the words before she can hide it, no armor.
CRITICAL ANTI-COLLAPSE: do NOT make all 5 sound like one archetype voice. Each card stays its OWN distinct move (an escalation is still an escalation, a boundary still a boundary, silence still wordless); friction + voice only color the DELIVERY. The 5 must remain 5 genuinely different CHOICES — if they read as five versions of the same impulse, you have failed. Against-the-grain (COSTLY) cards should feel especially charged; do NOT smooth them into the natural ones.
OUTPUT FORMAT (CRITICAL — follow EXACTLY): return EXACTLY 5 lines, one per archetype, and NOTHING else — no JSON, no braces, no preamble, no markdown, no quotation marks around the fields. Each line is the archetype name, the action, then the dialogue, separated by ||| (three pipes):
TEMPTATION ||| <action: max 12 words, specific physical act> ||| <dialogue: max 15 words>
BOUNDARY ||| <action> ||| <dialogue>
CONFESSION ||| <action> ||| <dialogue>
REVERSAL ||| <action> ||| <dialogue>
SILENCE ||| <stillness-based action> ||| <empty, or a single sound such as mm>
Use ||| ONLY as the field separator — never inside an action or dialogue. Apostrophes, commas, and punctuation inside the dialogue are FINE and need NO escaping.

Each entry MUST:
- Reference actual details from the scene (location, objects, on-stage characters)
- Match the Earnest tone
- Be more specific than generic templates
- Honor its archetype strategy absolutely
- DECK EXCLUSION (HARD): NEVER mention the protagonist's tarot deck, the cards, the Marseille deck, or "let the cards decide / draw a card" in ANY action or dialogue. The deck is a SEPARATE player mechanic (it has its own draw button), NOT a Say/Do option — keep it entirely out of every suggestion even though it appears in the scene. The protagonist holding the deck is NOT a reason to make handling it the action — suggest a REAL in-world action instead (use the scene's actual props, the protagonist's body, her voice, or — on a phone call — hang up / lower the phone / pace / go silent on the line). FORBIDDEN: "set the deck down," "put the cards away," "push the deck aside," "slip the cards into my pocket," "I'm deciding this, not the cards," "before I draw a card," etc.
